articles.title: Mallacoota's recycling champions win Tidy Towns Litter Award

check.note: Written by the publisher from East Gippsland Shire Council's announcement.

sources.title: Mallacoota's recycling champions score a Tidy Towns Litter Award

body: Some good news to start the month. Friends of Mallacoota and [Mallacoota Foreshore Holiday Park](/listing/mallacoota-foreshore-holiday-park.html) have won the 2026 Keep Australia Beautiful Victoria **Tidy Towns Litter Award** for their Container Deposit Scheme program. The award was presented this week at the Tidy Towns and Cities Sustainability Awards at Rydges Melbourne.
Anyone who has been here in January knows the problem. Our town of about 1,100 permanent residents can swell to as many as 10,000 people over summer, and the bins feel it.

The fix is simple and very Mallacoota. The holiday park puts out trailers where guests can drop their CDS-eligible cans and bottles. Friends of Mallacoota volunteers collect them and run them down to the town's container return point, and the refunds go towards conservation work in and around Croajingolong National Park.

It helps the return point too. Ours is one of the more remote in Victoria, and because the volunteers spread their collections across the year, it isn't swamped with a whole summer's worth of containers at once.
Congratulations to everyone involved, from the volunteers to the park staff and every camper who saved a can. And thanks to Keep Australia Beautiful Victoria for the recognition.
Source: [East Gippsland Shire Council on Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/eastgippyshire/), 1 October 2026.

articles.title: Mallacoota P-12 students visit Parliament House
body: Students from Mallacoota P-12 College visited Parliament House during a recent school trip to Canberra.

Federal Member for Gippsland Darren Chester met the group, including school captains Zoe Jakovljevic and Archie Brownlie, and talked with them about how Federal Parliament works and their time in Canberra.
Source: Snowy River Mail, 4 October 2026, https://snowyrivermail.com.au/19032/chester-welcomes-students-to-parliament/

articles.title: Fire Danger Period starts today in East Gippsland
body: The CFA's Fire Danger Period took effect at 1am on Monday 5 October across East Gippsland Shire, including Mallacoota, and Wellington Shire. It starts two weeks earlier than last season, with the CFA citing very dry conditions, high fuel loads, low soil moisture and more escaped burn-offs.

Burning off now needs a written permit (firepermits.vic.gov.au), and lighting a fire in the open without one can bring a fine of more than $21,800 and/or 12 months' jail. Check what you can and can't do at cfa.vic.gov.au/can or on 1800 226 226.
Source: CFA, 29 September 2026, https://news.cfa.vic.gov.au/victorian-fire-season-to-officially-begin

articles.title: Flatty Classic sold out for 23-25 October
body: The Daiwa Mallacoota Flatty Classic is sold out for 23-25 October, with every team spot filled and the draw done - 51 teams across 17 divisions. Comp HQ is Scallywags Bar on Allan Drive, overlooking the main boat ramp, for a three-day catch-measure-release, lure-only flathead tournament with bream and mulloway side pots. Organisers have a prefish ban in place, asking anglers to stay off the water until the 23rd.
Source: Fishing Classics (Mallacoota Flatty Classic), as at 12-13 October 2026, https://fishingclassics.com.au/competitions/mallacoota-flatty-classic-2026

articles.title: Adam Lalor wins Hobie series finale at Mallacoota
body: The Hobie Kayak Fishing Series wrapped up its 2026 season at Mallacoota on 10-11 October with the BerleyPro Round 10, fishing for bream out of the Main Boat Ramp. NSW angler Adam Lalor won with six fish for 4.97 kg. Simon Morley (NSW, 4.47 kg) came second and Joseph Gardner (WA, 4.37 kg) third. Peter Nord won the Masters division (3.70 kg), Leanne Cowan won Women's (1.64 kg) and James Kilpatrick Jr won Youth (1.26 kg). Across both days the field weighed in 175 fish for 110.77 kg.
Source: Hobie Kayak Fishing Series, 11 Oct 2026, https://www.hobiefishing.com.au/round/berleypro-round-10-mallacoota-vic-2026/

articles.title: Genoa History Park opens on 19 October
body: The Genoa District Community Group will officially open the Genoa History Park on Monday 19 October, from 11.30am to 1.30pm, at 4655 Princes Highway, opposite the Genoa Community Hall. The park is built on the site of the old Genoa school and came out of the community's 2019-20 bushfire recovery plan. It has a shed for the town's firefighting and SES trailers, new landscaping, a picnic shelter and signs telling the town's history, and it completes the 4km return loop walk from the Genoa Campground. Everyone is welcome, and it was funded by private donations, Fire to Flourish, the Victorian Government, the Foundation for Rural & Regional Renewal and East Gippsland Shire Council.
Source: Snowy River Mail, 6 October 2026, https://snowyrivermail.com.au/19039/genoa-history-park-opening/

articles.title: Free tourism workshop coming to Mallacoota on 14 October
body: Destination Gippsland is bringing its tourism industry workshop roadshow to Mallacoota on Wednesday 14 October, from 11am to 2pm. The session covers current market trends, international travel trade, working with the media and how Destination Gippsland uses AI, with regional case studies, a Q&A and a networking session to finish. It's free for operators with an active Australian Tourism Data Warehouse (ATDW) listing and $54 for everyone else. Registration links are on the Destination Gippsland industry portal.
Source: Snowy River Mail, 6 October 2026, https://snowyrivermail.com.au/19017/future-proofing-local-tourism/

articles.title: Hooded plover patrols return to Mallacoota beaches
body: The Conservation Regulator's Operation Save our Hoodies is back for its sixth season with Parks Victoria and BirdLife Australia. Patrols this nesting season stretch east from Lakes Entrance to Cape Conran and Mallacoota. Fewer than 700 hooded plovers are left in Victoria, and last season only 68 of 220 hatched chicks survived to become juveniles. Beachgoers are asked to follow the signs, give the birds plenty of space and keep dogs away from fenced nests until the season ends in March. Disturbing a hooded plover, its nest or its eggs can bring fines of up to $10,455, and disturbance can be reported to Crime Stoppers on 1800 333 000.

Source: South Gippsland Sentinel-Times, 25 September 2026, https://www.sgst.com.au/patrols-return-to-shield-rare-hoodies-nesting-on-south-gippsland-beaches/ (also TRFM, 24 September 2026, https://trfm.com.au/articles/nesting-season/)
